concerns.location: plan.md:T004 / research.md §2 (YOLOv8 for faces and weapons)
concerns.text: YOLOv8's standard pretrained COCO weights have no 'weapon' class (only 'knife' and 'sports ball' are near-neighbors). The plan says weights 'auto-download from ultralytics CDN' with no mention of a weapon-capable model or class mapping. If default COCO weights are used, weapon ROIs will be systematically undetected or mis-detected, invalidating the weapon-ROI arm of the analysis (and the scene_complexity covariate). Specify which model/classes map to 'weapon' and how detection quality will be validated, or restrict claims to face ROIs.

first_fixation_prob is a binary per-trial event (first fixation lands in ROI or not), yet the plan fits a Gaussian linear mixed model for all three outcomes. A LMM on a 0/1 outcome with ~200 items is statistically inappropriate; a logistic GLMM (or aggregated per-stimulus proportion with binomial weights) is needed for hypothesis (b). The plan mentions Gamma GLMM only for dwell time. Specify the link/function for the first-fixation outcome.

Power analysis uses 'parameters from actual aligned N' with fixed f=0.15, ICC≈0.1 — post-hoc power from realized N is acknowledged as limited, good, but the plan does not state the simulation generates data under the *alternative* using the fitted model structure (random intercepts for participants AND items). Clarify the simulation mirrors the crossed random-effects design, otherwise the power estimate answers a different design than the one fitted.

FR-001 mandates 'pixel-wise salience maps ... using the DeepGaze II model in CPU-only mode', but the plan (T003) computes salience with OpenCV spectral residual + center-surround fallback. The deviation is justified (T003 unverifiable) and logged in Complexity Tracking, but the spec FR text is unchanged, so the plan does not cover FR-001 as written. Update spec FR-001 (and US-1/Assumptions referencing DeepGaze II) to name the CPU spectral-residual method so plan and spec agree.

FR-008 mandates 'an ensemble of YOLOv8 (for faces) and Detectron2 (for weapons)'; the plan drops Detectron2 and uses YOLOv8 for both classes (T004, Complexity Tracking). The plan element has no matching FR as specified. Amend FR-008 (and the Assumption about the ensemble) to reflect single-detector YOLOv8 segmentation.

concerns.location: research.md §2 Dataset Strategy; plan.md T004 / FR-008
concerns.text: YOLOv8 with standard pretrained weights cannot detect the 'weapon' ROI class. The default ultralytics release channel ships COCO-pretrained weights, and COCO has no 'weapon' category (only 'knife'; no 'gun'/'rifle' class). The plan's claim that 'YOLOv8 alone covers both face and weapon detection' is therefore wrong for the pretrained models it plans to auto-download. The plan must either (a) name a specific weapon-detection model/weights that is actually available and CPU-runnable, (b) restrict the weapon ROI to COCO-detectable classes (e.g. 'knife') with the limitation logged, or (c) rely on pre-segmented masks if the dataset provides them.

concerns.location: research.md §2 (ds003123 'No verified source'); plan.md Constitution Check Principle I; quickstart.md Prerequisites
concerns.text: The entire pipeline depends on a dataset with no verified accessible source: research.md states 'No verified source. None of the URLs in the verified-datasets block corresponds to this dataset' and access is 'Manual placement'. This directly conflicts with Constitution Principle I (results reproducible on a fresh GitHub Actions runner, datasets fetched from the same canonical source every run). The plan should either identify and cite a verified, reachable source for the eye-tracking data (or an equivalent open dataset), or explicitly document that end-to-end reproducibility is conditional on manual data placement and state what the recorded artifacts will be in the dataset-absent case beyond a DATA_MISSING_001 abort.

T003 replaces FR-001's mandated 'DeepGaze II model' with OpenCV spectral residual, but unlike the FR-008 deviation (documented in Complexity Tracking), the FR-001 substitution has no Complexity Tracking entry or explicit deviation note. Add one so the plan's self-declared deviations are complete and consistent with its own tracking table.

output.schema.yaml lists `power_estimate` as a REQUIRED property, but data-model.md §3.2's 'Properties (all required)' enumeration omits `power_estimate` entirely. The two documents disagree on the results.json contract; add it to data-model.md.

concerns.location: data-model.md:§1 Entities vs plan.md Project Structure / T004
concerns.text: The plan produces `masks/*.png` and `mask_metadata.csv` (T004, data flow §2), but the data model defines no Mask/ROIMask entity and no schema for mask_metadata.csv. Every interim artifact the plan promises should be named by the data model; add a Mask entity (stimulus_id, roi_type, mask_path, confidence, status).

T004 places YOLOv8 image-derived ROI segmentation inside `code/eye_tracking/segment_roi.py`, and T006 derives `salience_score` as mean salience within those ROI masks. Constitution VI requires predictor (image stream) and outcome (gaze stream) processing to be independent; the predictor's ROI definition living in the eye_tracking module blurs that boundary. Either move segment_roi.py to a neutral/image module or document in the Constitution Check why this does not violate Principle VI.

Spectral-residual salience is computed from the Fourier amplitude spectrum of the grayscale image — i.e., it is mathematically a function of the same low-level luminance/contrast statistics entered as covariates (FR-009). Regressing salience on outcomes while 'controlling for' its own inputs risks over-adjustment/attenuation and makes the covariate-adjusted coefficient hard to interpret. The plan should state this limitation and report both covariate-adjusted and unadjusted salience effects.

No center-bias control. Spectral-residual and center-surround saliency maps both have strong central peaks, and eye-tracking fixations are also strongly center-biased; this shared bias can produce a spurious salience–dwell association — a canonical confound in this literature. Add an explicit control (e.g., center-of-image distance covariate or annulus-based baseline comparison).

first_fixation_prob is a binary event per trial (first fixation lands in ROI or not), yet Model A is a linear MixedLM treating it as a continuous DV. A logistic GLMM (or per-participant/ROI aggregation with weights) is the appropriate link for this outcome; the plan only mentions log-transform/Gamma for dwell time.
